report.summary: Reviewed archive.py chunk 1 of 1: 30 claims enumerated, 27 kept, 3 uncheckable; 4 observations noted.
risks: OUTCOME_RANK | medium | Unknown outcomes sort with rank -1, below 'task_invalid'; docstring says 'Unknown outcomes sort worst' — consistent but worth verifying intent matches policy. | Check callers that rely on unknown outcomes being worst.
record_attempt | low | meta is not truncated; a candidate-influenced meta dict could grow unbounded, contradicting 'BOUNDED' claim. | Inspect callers to see if meta is candidate-controlled.
record_attempt | low | unfixed is truncated to 20 but no length cap on each string; a single test id could be huge. | Check if test ids are bounded elsewhere.
load_attempts | low | Malformed lines are skipped silently; if the file format changes, it will report 'absent' rather than 'unreadable'. | Confirm if silent skip is intended for all parse errors.

handoff.purpose: Review archive module for docstring/comment claims against actual code.

claims.text: This module stores a hash plus a TRUNCATED, caller-supplied summary, and it never reads a candidate's files.
claims.why: Attempt has patch_digest (hash) and summary (truncated), no file I/O on candidates; only reads/writes the archive file.

claims.text: DETERMINISTIC BY DEFAULT. Every draw here takes an explicit rng, so a run is reproducible and a test can pin the selection instead of retrying until it passes.
claims.why: sample_inspirations accepts rng parameter and defaults to random.Random(0).

claims.text: BOUNDED. Every field that a candidate can influence is length-capped on the way IN, so a pathological error message cannot grow the file without limit.
claims.why: summary is truncated, unfixed truncated to 20 items, but meta is not truncated; meta is a dict that could contain arbitrary candidate-influenced strings.

claims.text: NOTHING HERE SPENDS, WRITES CODE, OR GATES ANYTHING
claims.why: No calls to providers, no code generation, no gate logic; only file I/O for the archive.

claims.text: This module appends JSON lines to a file the caller names, and reads them back.
claims.why: record_attempt appends, load_attempts reads.

claims.text: It calls no model, imports no provider, touches no lane, and is not wired into any gate or promotion path.
claims.why: No such imports or references in this chunk.

claims.text: A caller that renders these into a prompt is responsible for the egress decision -- this module makes that easy to audit by ensuring there is exactly one field to audit.
claims.why: Attempt has only 'summary' as free text; other fields are structured.

claims.text: Mirrored deliberately rather than imported: `daedalus.eval.correctness` is a heavyweight module and this one is meant to stay a leaf. `tests/test_kairos_archive.py::test_outcome_vocabulary_matches_the_evaluator` pins the agreement, so drift is a test failure rather than a silent divergence.
claims.why: The test file is not in this chunk; cannot verify the test exists or pins agreement.

claims.text: Upstream config.py:268-269 -- num_top_programs=3, num_diverse_programs=2.
claims.why: Upstream file not provided; cannot verify line numbers.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT a program record. There is no code field and there will not be one -- see the module docstring on egress.
claims.why: Attempt dataclass has no code field.

claims.text: Where this sits in the outcome ordering. Unknown outcomes sort worst.
claims.why: rank returns -1 for unknown outcomes, which is less than all defined ranks (0-4).

claims.text: Stable short identity for a change, so duplicates are recognisable.
claims.why: Uses SHA-256 truncated to 16 hex chars; deterministic.

claims.text: A digest, not the patch. Two candidates that produced byte-identical changes are the same attempt for inspiration purposes, and saying so costs 16 hex characters instead of a diff.
claims.why: Function returns a hash, not the patch.

claims.text: Append-only and one JSON object per line, so a crashed run leaves a readable prefix rather than a corrupt document, and two processes appending cannot interleave a half-record into another's.
claims.why: Uses 'a' mode and writes a single json.dumps line; OS append is atomic for small writes on most systems, but this is not guaranteed; however the claim is about interleaving half-records, which is mitigated by single write call.

claims.text: Truncation happens HERE, not at the call site, so there is a single place that decides how much candidate-influenced text is allowed to persist.
claims.why: record_attempt calls _truncate on summary; no other truncation in module.

claims.text: Read the notebook. Never raises.
claims.why: Catches OSError for read_text and ValueError/TypeError/AttributeError for parsing; no other exceptions escape.

claims.text: A line that will not parse is SKIPPED rather than fatal: this is advisory data, and a torn final line from a killed process must not take down the run that comes after it.
claims.why: The except clause catches parse errors and continues.

claims.text: Pick a few prior attempts worth showing the next one.
claims.why: Function returns a tuple of attempts.

claims.text: Adapted from upstream database.py::_sample_inspirations: take the best few, then FILL THE REST WITH VARIETY rather than with more of the best.
claims.why: Implementation selects elite then diverse from remaining, preferring fresh outcomes.

claims.text: Upstream draws its variety from neighbouring MAP-Elites cells; without a feature grid we approximate the same intent by preferring attempts whose OUTCOME class is not already represented, which is the coarsest honest diversity signal available from data we actually have.
claims.why: The code separates fresh and stale based on outcome coverage.

claims.text: DEDUPLICATION BY DIGEST. Five candidates that made byte-identical changes are one lesson, not five, and showing the same failing patch five times is how a loop talks itself into a rut.
claims.why: The loop skips attempts whose patch_digest is already seen.

claims.text: exclude_digest drops the attempt currently being worked on, so a candidate is never offered itself as inspiration.
claims.why: The seen set is initialized with exclude_digest, and attempts with that digest are skipped.

claims.text: Failures are as instructive as successes here -- a regressed attempt tells the next one what not to touch -- so this does NOT filter to winners.
claims.why: No filtering based on outcome; all attempts are included in pool.

claims.text: Ordering is best-first and fully deterministic given rng.
claims.why: Sorted by (-rank, -ts, attempt_id) which is deterministic, and rng is seeded if not provided.

claims.text: Best first; ties broken by recency, then by id so the order is total.
claims.why: The sort key is (-a.rank, -a.ts, a.attempt_id), which is a total order.

claims.text: Variety: prefer outcome classes the elite slice did not already show.
claims.why: fresh list is built from outcomes not in covered set.

claims.text: Keep the TAIL: a traceback's last lines carry the actual error, and the head is import noise.
claims.why: _truncate returns '...' + text[-(limit-3):], which is the tail.

claims.text: A candidate-influenced string. Capped on the way in, because the failure mode is a 40MB traceback appended once per iteration.
claims.why: MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS is 600 and _truncate enforces it in record_attempt.

claims.text: NO MAP-Elites feature grid, NO islands, NO migration. ADR-015 P8 defers those, and they are second-order on top of a loop that does not iterate yet.
claims.why: No such machinery in this chunk.

claims.text: WE STORE A DIGEST, THEY STORE THE CODE. ... An archive that holds candidate source is an egress vector ... This module stores a hash plus a TRUNCATED, caller-supplied summary, and it never reads a candidate's files.
claims.why: Attempt has patch_digest (hash) and summary (truncated); no code field, no candidate file reads.

observations.what: The module docstring claims 'Every field that a candidate can influence is length-capped on the way in', but the meta dict is not truncated or capped.
record_attempt truncates unfixed to 20 items, but does not cap the length of each individual test id string.
load_attempts silently skips malformed lines, which could hide file format changes; the docstring says 'Never raises' but does not mention silent skipping as a feature.
The claim that two processes appending cannot interleave a half-record is not strictly guaranteed by Python's file write; it depends on OS atomicity of append writes.
